inbox.subject: Incident: household summary sent to the wrong family
inbox.body:
Alex,

Last night at 9:40pm Lucas Ferreira, one of our Family care leads, emailed the monthly household summary for Margaret Oduya to the wrong family. Margaret has been a member since 2022. The email went to the Halvorsen household, who are also on Lucas's caseload. Autocomplete picked the wrong contact.

What was exposed: Margaret's name and her care plan (medication schedule, mobility notes, upcoming appointments by type). No financial data, no address, no account or insurance numbers.

What we've done: Lucas flagged it himself at 10:15pm. Tom Halvorsen replied at 11:02pm confirming he deleted it and did not forward it. I have that in writing. I've disabled autocomplete for external addresses on care lead mail as of 5:30am.

What I need from you: a decision on notifying Margaret and her daughter today. My recommendation is that we call them today, with Lucas's manager on the line, and follow with a written letter. Outside counsel (Priscilla Vance) agrees we should notify promptly even if this falls below a formal reporting threshold. I've put 8:30am on your calendar.

Nadia

inbox.subject: Re: Incident: household summary sent to the wrong family
inbox.body:
Nadia, Alex,

The care plan includes memory care notes, which families tend to find more upsetting than a billing slip would. I'd support telling Margaret's daughter today, by phone, before she hears it any other way. Happy to join the 8:30am.

Sofia

inbox.subject: Board deck draft: due tomorrow
inbox.body:
Alex,

Reminder the draft goes to board members tomorrow, Wednesday. I've updated the finance slides: ARR at $17.8M, year end plan $19.0M, forecast gap $1.2M. Still need your narrative on the gap and on Harborline launch pace (1,600 households entering setup in January on a full launch vs 800 we can set up from January 1 and keep the promise).

See you at 11:30am.

Julian

inbox.subject: Tuesday sync agenda
inbox.body:
Team,

Agenda for 10am:
1. Boston overnight: last recurrence ran 3.2 hours, backlog peaked at 164 handoffs, down to 58 by 5am. Sanjay to walk through the queue patch (1 week roadmap slip).
2. Hiring: 12 care lead hires planned for Q1, 3 offers accepted, active pipeline down 17 percent month over month.
3. Harborline January capacity.

Jordan

inbox.subject: Harborline: Diane wants a phased plan
inbox.body:
Alex,

Diane Coleridge called this afternoon. Owen Pryce is pushing for full rollout to all 40,000 employees on January 1. Diane is open to phasing if we bring a clear plan Thursday. That's $2.9M of new ARR at $6 per employee per month either way. Let's lock our position at 4:30pm.

Tomás
